detect.title: What We Detect
detect.description: 30+ invisible Unicode characters commonly used as AI watermarks or that leak from AI tools. Each is shown with its code point, name, and category.

items.title: U+200B — Zero-Width Space
items.description: Invisible space used to break words. Common ChatGPT watermark.

items.title: U+200C / U+200D — Non-Joiner & Joiner
items.description: Invisible characters controlling glyph joining, heavily used in emoji sequences.

items.title: U+2060 — Word Joiner
items.description: Zero-width no-break space; prevents line break without showing visible width.

items.title: U+FE00 – U+FE0F — Variation Selectors
items.description: 16 invisible formatting characters that select glyph variants of preceding characters.

items.title: U+200E / U+200F — LTR & RTL Marks
items.description: Invisible directionality marks. Abused in phishing for visual spoofing.

items.title: U+202A–U+202E — Directional Embedding
items.description: Force LTR/RTL ordering. Heavily abused in URL spoofing and homoglyph attacks.

items.title: U+2066–U+2069 — Directional Isolates
items.description: Isolate following text into LTR/RTL direction. Modern replacement for embedding.

items.title: U+00A0 — No-Break Space
items.description: Looks like a regular space but prevents line wrapping. Breaks CMS parsers.

items.title: U+202F — Narrow No-Break Space
items.description: Half-width no-break space. Often leaks from AI tools and French typography.

items.title: U+205F — Medium Mathematical Space
items.description: Invisible math spacing used in formulas; rarely needed in prose.

items.title: U+2007–U+200A — Figure/Punct/Thin/Hair Spaces
items.description: Specialized invisible spaces that break HTML whitespace normalization.

items.title: U+00AD — Soft Hyphen
items.description: Invisible hyphen made visible only when wrapping breaks the word.

items.title: U+2061–U+2064 — Invisible Operators
items.description: Function application, invisible times, separator, and plus from math expressions.

items.title: U+2028 / U+2029 — Line & Paragraph Separators
items.description: Break characters that are NOT newlines. Break JSON and SQL inserts.

items.title: U+FEFF — Zero-Width No-Break Space (BOM)
items.description: Byte Order Mark; invisible at start of text but visible mid-string.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Everything you need to know about detecting AI watermarks and hidden Unicode characters.

items.question: What is an AI watermark?
items.answer: An AI watermark is an invisible or hard-to-spot pattern embedded in text generated by models like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. It often uses hidden Unicode characters such as zero-width spaces (U+200B) or variation selectors (U+FE00–U+FE0F) that look empty but uniquely identify the source. Our AI watermark detector scans for these characters and lets you clean them from your text.

items.question: How does this AI watermark detector work?
items.answer: The watermark checker scans your text locally in the browser for 30+ invisible Unicode characters including zero-width spaces, directional marks, BOM, and variation selectors. When suspicious characters are found, an optional server-side AI review offers a second opinion with a 0–100 confidence score and a short reason. The scanner never stores your input.

items.question: Can the ChatGPT watermark detector find ChatGPT watermarks specifically?
items.answer: Yes. The detector covers the exact Unicode characters most commonly reported as ChatGPT watermarks, including U+200B (zero-width space), U+200C (non-joiner), U+200D (joiner), and U+2060 (word joiner). If you want a deeper walkthrough, read our ChatGPT watermark detector guide on the blog.

items.question: How do I remove AI watermarks from text?
items.answer: Paste your text into the input box and click Analyze. When hidden characters are found, click 'Copy Clean Text' to instantly copy the cleaned version with all invisible watermarks removed. For a step-by-step walkthrough, see our guide on how to remove AI watermarks from text.

items.question: Is this AI watermark detector free?
items.answer: Yes. The ai watermark detector free plan gives you 5 anonymous checks per day without signup. Sign up for free to unlock 50 checks per day and prepare for future Pro features like batch file processing and API access.

items.question: Is my text stored or sent anywhere?
items.answer: No. Your text is scanned locally in your browser. It is only forwarded to the optional server-side AI review when suspicious patterns are found, and even then it is never persisted. By default the front-end scan already covers most needs.

items.question: What is a zero-width space and why does it matter?
items.answer: A zero-width space (U+200B) is an invisible Unicode character that breaks words without rendering a visible gap. It can break CMS parsing, database inserts, screen readers, and search indexing. Use our zero width space remover to strip them automatically.

items.question: Can professors detect AI watermarks in student essays?
items.answer: Academic integrity workflows increasingly use hidden Unicode characters as one signal of AI-assisted writing. Professors can run a submission through this invisible watermark detector to spot zero-width characters that would not appear in normal typed text.
